newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply higher on spec buying.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply higher on spec buying.

text.p: NYCE cotton ended sharply higher on speculative buying, confounding the market after it had been called to open lower because of poor USDA export sales figures, traders said.

Weekly USDA export figures, released before trading began, showed that sales in the week ended November 14 were a net 95,000 running bales. Traders had expected 200,000 to 300,000 bales but the market firmed from the opening bell.
A floor source said U.S. cotton was pricing itself out of the market. Cotton prices were lower during the week covered by USDA data, but had moved even higher by now.
Traders said there was good speculative buying which triggered a rash of stops letting the market run up to a high of 75.90 cents per pound for the most active March contract.
"I am pretty sure the market is still short right now," the floor source said.
Friday is the first notice day for the December contract which expires on December 6.
March cotton settled 1.50 cents firmer at 75.73 cents per pound, traded 75.90 to 73.75 cents.
Meanwhile Brazil's Futures and Commodities Exchange said its own cotton futures contract will be launched on Nov 22.
